description:
Markdown memory files work for one agent. They break when many agents, users and teams share them. Cognee founder Vasilije Markovic explains why at 1:21.

What Cognee built instead: a thin agent memory layer that runs on Postgres and scores 79% on the BEAM memory benchmark.

From his slide: "We can't move forward with MD files. We need compliance, predictability and control."

In this talk:
- Why MD files fail as AI agent memory at scale (concurrency, locking, indexing)
- Ontologies: the domain knowledge that sits between your agent and your data
- One small Postgres per agent, team or user ("memory box")
- Session memory vs permanent memory, and promoting memory from agent to user to team to org
- 79% accuracy on the BEAM memory benchmark
- A small model runtime, so building the memory graph needs no OpenAI or Anthropic calls
- Self-improving memory: re-weighting embeddings instead of hard deletes
